# Lynn Conway
Lynn Conway was a pioneering computer scientist and engineer who revolutionized the design of very-large-scale integration (VLSI) systems. Along with Carver Mead, she developed the Mead–Conway VLSI design methodology, which introduced dimensionless, scalable design rules that simplified chip design and allowed universities and small companies to access state-of-the-art technology through the Metal Oxide Semiconductor Implementation Service (MOSIS). Her work fostered the growth of the electronic design automation industry and established the foundry model for chip manufacturing, leading to her induction into the National Inventors Hall of Fame and numerous accolades, including the IEEE Computer Pioneer Award.
Beyond her technical achievements, Conway is a prominent figure in transgender rights activism. After publicly disclosing her gender transition in 1999, she became a vocal advocate for trans rights, employment protections in the high-technology sector, and the elimination of the pathologization of transgender individuals. She co-founded the website "Transsexual Women's Successes" to provide role models and medical resources, served as a cast member in the first all-transgender performance of *The Vagina Monologues* , and was named one of the "Stonewall 40 trans heroes" in 2009. Conway passed away on June 9, 2024, at the age of 86.
